content.comment_body: Good morning, I need assistance connecting an RS485 temperature and humidity sensor to port AB on the [product_name]. I've configured Modbus RTU for RS485, baud rate 9600, with 1 start bit, 8 data bits, no parity, and 1 stop bit. I’ve set up the data transfer table with VW2 mapped to HR, starting at 30, length 1, Unit ID 1. In [product_name] software, I added the module and Modbus with an analogue network input, but no data is being received. The sensor datasheet is attached. Any help would be appreciated.

What is the status of the DIAG LED on your [product_name] module? It should be green. How is your [product_name] connected to the module? For example, if you’re using port1, the P1 LED should also be green. I’m assuming you are using Modbus TCP on your [product_name] with [version_no]. If that is the case, both Modbus and S7 communication need to be enabled in [product_name].

Thank you for your response. The P1 LED on the [product_name] module is green and connected to the [product_name], while the P2 LED is green and connected to the laptop. Modbus TCP is enabled. I originally enabled S7 communication, but disabled it since I’m now using Modbus TCP. I selected analogue input since I have a temperature and humidity sensor. The manual suggests using Hex code, so I’m unsure whether my input type is correct. During online diagnostics, the only value displayed is 0.0. Thanks, [user_name]

For Modbus TCP with [product_name] [version_no], you must activate S7 communication in addition to Modbus. P1 and P2 LEDs are good. Make sure the DIAG LED on the [product_name] module is green; if it’s off, there might be an issue such as a power supply problem. The module requires a 12/24V power supply (range: 10.2 to 28.8V DC). Without power, the DIAG LED will be off. [product_name] processes bits and integers (2 bytes). Using the conversion block, you can handle 4- and 8-byte floating point values as well. However, single bytes and strings can’t be processed directly. The hex values mentioned for your sensor seem like strings, and it’s unclear if I/O addresses or holding registers are used. Since holding registers are 2 bytes, I suspect I/O addresses are in use.
Consider using a PC with a USB RS485 interface and software to configure and read data from the RTU sensor. This will help verify sensor functionality. [url]

Hi, start by checking whether your sensor's value appears in the [product_name] memory. You can use the RESTful API Interface for this. If enabled in [product_name], enter this URL in your browser: [url] (replace with IP address and VW30 register as noted). The browser should show the sensor value. Afterward, set up data exchange between VW30 of the [product_name] and [product_name] using ModbusTCP or S7. Typically, configuring [product_name] as the server makes these changes faster than repeatedly loading programs onto [product_name]. Hope this helps.
Currently, only a zero value is displayed. Is it possible to set HR to 0?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing challenges when trying to interface an RS485 temperature and humidity sensor with the [product_name] module through Modbus RTU and TCP protocols, using [product_name] and [product_name] software. The main issues involve configuring the correct input type—especially when handling hexadecimal values and string formats— and obtaining readings beyond zero. Feedback from others clarifies technical limitations of [product_name] in processing certain data formats and highlights necessary module and communication settings, but the problem of getting valid sensor data remains unresolved.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects to reliably read, process, and display sensor values in [product_name] software via the [product_name] module, with proper data communication over Modbus RTU/TCP, regardless of the sensor's data format.
